added.name: Verno
added.long_description: Every refinery, chip fab and power plant is built from thousands of engineering documents that are supposed to agree, and engineers still keep them in sync by hand. Verno is AI for how the physical world gets built. An engineer describes a change, and Verno edits the P&ID in the native CAD file, carries the change through line lists and other downstream documents, and checks every one against engineering rules before the engineer approves it. On drawings already issued for construction, it has caught errors like one tank with three different design pressures across three documents. We're starting with process EPCs in oil and gas, chemicals, semiconductors, pharma, and food and beverage, then expanding into water and power.
added.one_liner: AI engineering industrials like chip fabs, refineries and power plants

Goodshelf is an AI-native online retailer built to help people and AI shopping agents discover, understand, recommend, and buy the right products.

Goodshelf sells curated products across electronics, home goods, travel, beauty, furniture, everyday essentials, and more. Unlike traditional online marketplaces, Goodshelf prioritizes product quality, transparent comparisons, and evidence-backed recommendations over sponsored rankings and advertising.

Goodshelf brings together products from brands and suppliers, combining detailed product specifications, real-world use cases, independent reviews, testing insights, and evidence-based comparisons. We make pricing, availability, product strengths, limitations, and tradeoffs clear upfront, giving AI agents and consumers the information they need to evaluate alternatives and choose the products that best fit their needs.

Goodshelf is built for both human shoppers and AI agents like ChatGPT, Gemini, Muse, and Instinct. Our structured product catalog, machine-readable product pages, and agent-compatible shopping tools make it easier for AI assistants to research products, compare alternatives, and help customers complete purchases.

Our mission is to help AI agents find the right product for every consumer, while giving brands and suppliers a new distribution channel as shopping shifts toward AI.

long_description.before:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. Each comes from real, de-identified records (health data, industrial sensors, compute-cluster logs), in three families: personal agents, industry, and science and compute. The world keeps moving while the agent works, so the agent must keep learning: data arrive on a clock, and every answer is checked against what actually happened. In each family, the best frontier model averages below half, and models that train on our environments improve.

We specialise in time series because almost everything that matters is recorded that way: a heartbeat, a power grid, a factory line, a GPU cluster, an experiment. No person can turn thousands of moving signals at once into the state of a system and what happens next. AI can pass the bar exam, but it still can’t watch a system for weeks and act at the right moment. It learned from what people wrote down, in environments that freeze the world and abstract it to our understanding.

Time series let us ride the exponential. The world records new data every second and time keeps grading, so each generation of models gets harder, fresher tasks. We believe humans always strive to explore. Our mission is to build the infrastructure for that exploration: the layer of the AI stack where models keep improving, out into what no one understands yet.
long_description.after:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. AI has learned to reason over text and code. But most of what matters in the real world shows up as numbers that change every second: a heartbeat, a gearbox, a GPU cluster. No human can track thousands of signals at once, but AI should be able to.

In our environments, data streams in on a clock while the agent works, and every action is graded by what actually happened. Most AI training today teaches models to match human experts. We treat human performance as the floor. Each environment comes from real, de-identified records, in three task families: personal agents, industry, and science & compute.

Today, even the best frontier model averages under 50% on each family. Training an open model on our environments raised its full-solve rate on unseen tasks by 54% (from 25.6% to 39.5%), with no loss on general benchmarks. Our mission is to build the infrastructure that keeps AI climbing the frontier, long past human level in the real world.

long_description.after:
Plek is the AI company brain for private equity value creation. Upload an employee census, and Plek maps every person to a taxonomy of 50,000 jobs and 250,000 tasks, down to the time each task takes. It then analyzes spans and layers, org structure, footprint, compensation, functional fragmentation and AI exposure in parallel, and reconciles overlapping levers employee by employee so every dollar is traceable.

What takes a performance improvement team 6 to 8 weeks takes Plek under a minute. At a 3,600-person company, Plek found $30M in annual EBITDA levers, matching what a global PE advisory firm found in six weeks. Funds and advisories use Plek from due diligence to exit to run org value creation scenarios, from the platform or from their own AI agents via MCP.

Plek grew out of the MIT Work Analytics Lab, founded by CEO Pierre Bouquet during his MIT PhD. Long-term, Plek becomes the Celonis of the workforce: it continuously monitors the org and flags value creation levers as they appear.

one_liner.before: Maps what employees do and what it costs
one_liner.after: The AI company brain for PE value creation
